mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently compresses equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This is because ultra-low rates signal an accommodative monetary policy that boosts risk appetite and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE above 8% indicates a high unemployment rate, which is associated with weak economic growth and reduced corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The co-occurrence of a federal funds rate below 0.5% and CPIAUCSL below 220 indicates a stable monetary environment with moderate inflation, which historically has been associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This interaction is not captured by either variable alone.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5 AND CPIAUCSL < 220, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, defined by INDPRO > 100 and HOUST > 500, the economy is overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always negative when this regime condition is met.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO > 100 AND HOUST > 500, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A low industrial production (INDPRO < 100) is a consistent predictor of negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. The signal is always active, meaning the value of INDPRO is continuously monitored and used to predict returns, with the threshold of 100 defining the negative signal.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL above 220 indicates high inflation, which typically leads to monetary tightening and reduced equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 220, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The co-occurrence of strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 130000) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%) signals a robust labor market, which supports economic growth and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days. This interaction is not captured by either variable alone.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS > 130000 AND UNRATE < 5.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 8.0), a housing starts level below 500 (HOUST < 500) signals weak consumer demand and economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0 AND HOUST < 500, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
